title: Region normalization plan (unit economics + metering)
content:
Owner: Mei Lin (Data Eng)
Reviewers: Nadia Rahman (token metering), Cole Summers (cost attribution), Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Last updated: 2025-02-18

Why this doc exists
We currently have multiple “region” identifiers depending on the system:
- Cloud provider region: e.g., aws/us-east-1, gcp/us-central1, azure/westeurope
- Internal colo/POP labels: e.g., iad1, sjc1, fra1, lon1
- Kubernetes cluster names / deploy env aliases: e.g., prod-iad, prod-use1a, prod-euw1
- Billing / infra spend inputs: sometimes keyed by provider region, sometimes by fleet tag/colo

For the Unit Economics dashboard, we must be able to consistently group by region and reconcile:
(1) token metering (requests + output tokens), (2) capacity utilization signals, and (3) cost inputs (GPU rate card / spend allocation).

Goal
Introduce a canonical region dimension (canonical_region) that:
- is stable over time
- is low-cardinality
- can represent both cloud regions and Redwood-managed colos
- is consistently emitted in telemetry/metering and used in aggregation + dashboard queries

Non-goals (for this phase)
- Perfect “geo” accuracy (physical location) for every legacy label; we prioritize consistent grouping + reconciliation.
- Rewriting every service’s internal region naming. We normalize at ingestion/warehouse boundary.

Proposed canonical region scheme
We will standardize canonical_region as a single string with a namespace prefix:
- Cloud:   aws:<region> | gcp:<region> | azure:<region>
- Redwood colo/POP: rwd:<site>

Examples:
- aws:us-east-1
- aws:eu-west-1
- gcp:us-central1
- azure:westeurope
- rwd:iad1
- rwd:sjc1
- rwd:fra1

Rationale:
- Keeps cardinality bounded.
- Encodes provider in the value (no need for separate provider dimension to understand grouping).
- Avoids ambiguous “us-east” style labels.

Key definition
- raw_region: whatever the upstream system reports (may be null)
- raw_region_source: a small enum describing where raw_region came from
  - gateway (request routing)
  - runtime (serving cluster)
  - infra_billing (spend inputs)
  - warehouse_legacy (historical tables)
- canonical_region: normalized output used in all unit econ views + dashboards

Decision points / open questions
1) Do we ever want to collapse aws:us-east-1 and rwd:iad1 if they are physically co-located?
   Current recommendation: NO. Keep separate, because cost inputs and capacity differ.
2) How do we treat “edge” or “global” services (non-GPU) that sometimes emit region=global?
   Recommendation: canonical_region=global only for non-inference signals; for unit econ pipeline we should avoid allocating inference tokens to global.
3) How to treat multi-region routing/fallback?
   We attribute to the execution region (where tokens were generated), not the request ingress region.

Implementation plan (high level)
Phase 0: Inventory + mapping draft (this doc)
- Collect raw region values observed in:
  - metering events (streaming + non-streaming)
  - runtime metrics
  - cost/spend inputs
- Draft mapping table + note edge cases.

Phase 1: Authoritative mapping table in warehouse
- Create table: analytics.dim_region_mapping
- Update ingestion/ETL to join and emit canonical_region into the normalized metering fact table(s).
- Add “unknown/unmapped” handling with alerting.

Phase 2: Migrate downstream views + dashboard
- Update unit econ aggregation job to group by canonical_region.
- Update the Console API to expose canonical_region and a user-friendly display label.
- Backfill historical data for the dashboard time range (at least 2025Q1 per Finance needs).

Phase 3: Deprecate legacy fields
- Stop exposing raw/legacy region fields in dashboard paths.
- Keep raw_region for debugging only (restricted access / internal-only).

Data model proposal
Table: analytics.dim_region_mapping
Primary key: (raw_region_source, raw_region)

Columns:
- raw_region_source (string)  // small allowed set
- raw_region (string)         // raw input value; may include cluster names
- canonical_region (string)   // output value, per scheme above
- canonical_region_label (string) // UI-friendly label (e.g., “AWS us-east-1”, “Redwood IAD1”)
- environment (string)        // prod | staging | dev (optional; ideally prod-only)
- is_active (string)          // “true”/“false” as string; used to sunset legacy values
- first_seen_at (string)      // YYYY-MM-DD (populated by a daily job)
- last_seen_at (string)       // YYYY-MM-DD
- notes (string)              // freeform, link to threads/incidents

NOTE: This is a dimension table; changes should be reviewed (CODEOWNERS-style) because it affects exec reporting.

Draft mapping (initial)
Source: gateway
- raw_region=us-east-1                    -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1  notes=standard AWS
- raw_region=use1                        -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1  notes=legacy abbreviation
- raw_region=eu-west-1                   -> canonical_region=aws:eu-west-1        label=AWS eu-west-1
- raw_region=euw1                        -> canonical_region=aws:eu-west-1        label=AWS eu-west-1  notes=legacy abbreviation
- raw_region=us-central1                 -> canonical_region=gcp:us-central1      label=GCP us-central1
- raw_region=westeurope                  -> canonical_region=azure:westeurope     label=Azure westeurope
- raw_region=(null)                      -> canonical_region=unknown              label=Unknown        notes=should page if > threshold in prod

Source: runtime
- raw_region=prod-iad1                   -> canonical_region=rwd:iad1             label=Redwood IAD1   notes=runtime cluster alias
- raw_region=prod-sjc1                   -> canonical_region=rwd:sjc1             label=Redwood SJC1
- raw_region=prod-fra1                   -> canonical_region=rwd:fra1             label=Redwood FRA1
- raw_region=prod-euw1                   -> canonical_region=aws:eu-west-1        label=AWS eu-west-1  notes=runtime cluster deployed in AWS
- raw_region=prod-use1a                  -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1  notes=AZ suffix stripped
- raw_region=prod-use1b                  -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1
- raw_region=k8s-prod-use1-gpu           -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1  notes=cluster name normalization

Source: infra_billing
- raw_region=AWS:us-east-1               -> canonical_region=aws:us-east-1        label=AWS us-east-1  notes=billing export format
- raw_region=AWS:eu-west-1               -> canonical_region=aws:eu-west-1        label=AWS eu-west-1
- raw_region=RWD:IAD                     -> canonical_region=rwd:iad1             label=Redwood IAD1   notes=finance tag; confirm with Cole
- raw_region=RWD:SJC                     -> canonical_region=rwd:sjc1             label=Redwood SJC1

Edge cases to capture
- Mixed separators: “aws/us-east-1”, “aws:us-east-1”, “AWS us-east-1”. Plan: normalize raw_region with a small pre-parser per source before mapping lookup.
- AZ-level identifiers: “us-east-1a”, “use1-az1”. Plan: strip AZ suffix and map to region.
- “eu-west” (missing number). Plan: do not guess; set unknown and force mapping update.
- New regions: should not silently bucket into unknown for long; we want a tight feedback loop + alert.

Where normalization happens (recommended)
1) Ingestion layer (preferred)
- As metering events land in the warehouse (or in the streaming ETL), join to dim_region_mapping and write canonical_region into the normalized fact table.
Pros: downstream consumers all benefit; consistent.
Cons: requires careful rollout to avoid dropping events.

2) At query time (not recommended)
- Join mapping in every view.
Pros: fastest to prototype.
Cons: easy to get inconsistent; can hurt performance; harder to enforce completeness.

We will do (1) for unit economics paths.

Migration steps (detailed)
Step A — Add mapping table + seed values
- Create analytics.dim_region_mapping
- Seed with known raw values from:
  - last 14 days of metering logs
  - infra billing exports
  - runtime cluster config
- Ownership: Mei (implementation), Nadia (metering review), Cole (finance tags review)

Step B — Add canonical_region to normalized metering fact
- Add canonical_region column to normalized metering table (or equivalent view)
- Populate it via join to dim_region_mapping
- Set canonical_region=unknown if no match
- Emit a counter: unmapped_region_events by raw_region_source/raw_region (for alerting)

Step C — Update unit economics aggregation job
- Change grouping key from existing region fields to canonical_region
- Add validation: percent_unknown_region <= threshold (see SLO section)
- Add reconciliation check to ensure total tokens unchanged pre/post migration for a canary window

Step D — Backfill
- Backfill canonical_region for 2025Q1 to support Finance QTD/quarterly views
- Backfill strategy:
  - batch by day partitions
  - throttle to avoid warehouse overload (coordinate with SRE)

Step E — Deprecate
- Mark legacy region fields as “debug-only”
- Update dashboard/API to only show canonical_region_label

SLO / data quality checks
Targets (proposal; align with unit econ pipeline SLO doc):
- Freshness: canonical_region coverage available for >= 99% of hourly partitions within 2 hours
- Completeness: unknown canonical_region <= 0.5% of inference output tokens in prod (rolling 1h)
- Cardinality: distinct canonical_region values per day <= 200 (expected < 30)

Alerting
- Page (eng-oncall / observability): unknown canonical_region > 2% for 30 minutes OR sudden spike > 5x baseline
- Ticket-only: new raw_region value seen (first_seen) that maps to unknown for > 24h

Rollout plan
- Week 1: mapping table + join logic behind a feature flag in ETL; run in “shadow” mode writing canonical_region_shadow
- Week 2: switch unit econ aggregation to use canonical_region_shadow for comparison reports
- Week 3: promote canonical_region_shadow -> canonical_region; update dashboard grouping

Validation checklist
- Token totals match (within 0.1%) for a fixed time window before/after normalization
- Top regions by tokens are sensible; no large “unknown” bucket
- Finance cost inputs can be joined to canonical_region for rate card application (Cole sign-off)
- No dashboard regressions in drilldowns (region filter stable)

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Dropping rows due to inner joins on mapping table
  - Mitigation: left join + unknown bucket; alert on unknown rather than dropping
- Risk: Warehouse performance issues from frequent joins
  - Mitigation: materialize canonical_region in normalized facts; cluster/partition by date
- Risk: Mismatch between “execution region” and “billing region” for some capacity types
  - Mitigation: explicitly document allocation rules in cost attribution ADR; keep mapping table separate per source

Notes / TODOs
- TODO: Confirm finance tags “RWD:IAD” vs “rwd:iad1” mapping with Cole (by 2025-02-05)
- TODO: Audit runtime clusters that are in AWS but named like colos (prod-iad-aws) and decide canonical value
- TODO: Add a daily job to update first_seen_at/last_seen_at for mapping rows
- TODO: Document canonical_region in the token metering dimensions standard once finalized
